# Files kept from the tf-psa-crypto release archive, and where they land.
#
# Two columns, whitespace separated: the path inside src/vendor/tf-psa-crypto/
# first, then the path inside the upstream archive it is copied from.
# tools/vendor/fetch reads this file; tools/vendor/verify checks the tree
# against it in both directions.
#
# The list is not hand-written. It is the dependency closure of the sources
# that carry a symbol under src/zuc_crypto_config.h: compile all 77 upstream
# sources under that configuration, keep the 18 whose object defines anything
# (the rest are guarded down to empty translation units), and take every
# header those 18 actually include, with `cc -MM`. See
# .agents/stage-1-spike.md for the method and how to redo it after a release
# bump.
#
# The layout is flattened to two directories rather than mirroring upstream's
# six, and that is not tidiness. R CMD check rejects a tarball path over 100
# bytes, and upstream's own
#   drivers/builtin/include/mbedtls/private/crypto_adjust_config_enable_builtins.h
# is over it before src/vendor/ is even prefixed. It is the same limit that
# makes deep vendored trees fail to unpack on Windows. Two -I roots -- inc/
# for the public and private header hierarchies, lib/ for sources and their
# neighbouring private headers -- keep every path inside the limit, and
# tools/vendor/verify measures them so a future release cannot creep back
# over it. Within inc/ the mbedtls/, psa/ and tf-psa-crypto/ prefixes are
# upstream's own #include paths and cannot be touched.
